stem: This iconic monument with four grand arches and minarets, built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty (commemorating the end of a plague epidemic), stands at the heart of Hyderabad's old city. It is the:
explanation: The Charminar, built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, is Hyderabad's defining landmark — distinct from Golconda Fort (the Qutb Shahi dynasty's fortified citadel) or the Qutb Shahi Tombs (the dynasty's royal burial complex), though all are Qutb Shahi-era monuments in the same city.

stem: One of the world's largest one-man-collected museums, located in Hyderabad, houses an eclectic collection of art, sculpture, and artefacts (including the famous 'Veiled Rebecca' statue) assembled by a former Nizam-era statesman. This museum is the:
explanation: The Salar Jung Museum, built on the personal collection of Mir Yousuf Ali Khan (Salar Jung III), is renowned as one of the largest museums assembled by a single individual, distinct from India's other major state-run museums in Delhi, Chennai, and Kolkata.
